scope: Preserve retained expansion vendors and faction banner content while replacing singular NGE class assumptions with Publish 14.1 multi-profession skill ownership, preventing false Trader identity, and retiring the banner's Roadmap class buffs and combat proc from player gameplay.

eraEvidence.publish141Boundary: Publish 14.1 characters may independently learn multiple profession trees; novice skill ownership, not one class template, is authoritative.
findings: The retained helper previously returned Trader when none of its mapped PRE-CU profession predicates matched, so Marksman-, Brawler-, Scout-, and other unmapped characters were falsely classified as Traders.

The retained heroic vendor has separate class-indexed containers and copied its class-zero common rows into every existing class container, but previously opened only the first profession selected by a fixed priority order.
The existing item-local compatibility boundary maps retained Spy class ID 5 to outdoors_ranger_novice without making Ranger a global Spy identity.
Class-indexed retained inventory labels must resolve to localized Publish 14.1 profession roots rather than fabricated numeric NGE class keys.
Meatlump and Nova/Orion resource vendor tables contain only class-zero rows and therefore require no profession classification.

The retained GCW banner was the last singular NGE class consumer and applied one of nine Roadmap class buffs containing modified NGE primaries, Luck, expertise modifiers, or a server-only combat proc.
Pinned Publish 14.1 Core3 contains faction perks but no Roadmap class banner-buff system; retained banner items and visuals remain content, while their player stat/proc authority must fail closed.
